tasks.title: Complete direct LTE MQTT transport over PPP (CIP path unusable on unit)
tasks.description: CIP socket stack is not usable on the physical unit (A7670M7_V1.11.1 auto-enters PPP after AT+CGACT=1,1; historical +CIPOPEN evidence came from firmware A011B04A7670M7_F). Decision taken: ride MQTT over the PPP data channel - the path already proven by the NAT router. New baseline firmware/baseline/mqtt_ppp builds a raw lwIP TCP socket over pppos and does a byte-level MQTT exchange: fixed-frame CONNACK read by waiting in 500ms slices (the first 3s-slice timeout was aborting the outer 10s window), non-blocking send/recv with the UART feeder interleaved (blocking mode starved the link: 18.3s ENETUNREACH always) and frame builders corrected so the body sits right after the 1-byte remaining-length field (reserving 2 bytes left a garbage byte the broker dropped). Verified end-to-end: CONNACK rc=0, PUBLISH sent, payload observed by an independent mosquitto subscriber.
acceptance_criteria: Device logs MQTT-CONNECT sent
A CONNACK is received and parsed (expect 0x20 0x02 0x00 0x00)
A telemetry payload is observed by an independent subscriber on the target cluster
No bridge, tunnel, relay or cloudflared is involved at any point

evidence: mqtt_ppp serial capture 2026-09-30: 'CONNACK rc=0 sp=00', 'MARK-MQTT-CONNECTED', 'PUBLISH sent (71 bytes)', 'RESULT MQTT_PUBLISH PASS'
Independent subscriber (mosquitto_sub on Mac, broker.hivemq.com:1883) received: nomadlink/one/gps {\"src\":\"mqtt_ppp\",\"uptime_s\":32,\"phase\":\"RUNNING\"}
verification.reason: MQTT over PPP verified end to end via raw lwIP socket transport

tasks.title: Choose and document the firmware framework baseline (ESP-IDF vs Arduino)
tasks.description: Choose and document the firmware framework baseline. DECIDED: Option B, Arduino-ESP32 3.3.x as the product framework. The premise that made this hard is gone. NAPT is compiled into and exported from the shipped Arduino core (liblwip.a contains ip4_napt.c.obj and exports ip_napt_enable_netif/ip_napt_forward/ip_napt_recv; libesp_netif.a exports esp_netif_napt_enable; sdkconfig sets CONFIG_LWIP_IP_FORWARD, CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT, CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT_PORTMAP), so NAT is not ESP-IDF-only and REQ-004 no longer discriminates between the frameworks. PPP is already verified on Arduino (TASK-020) after three non-obvious fixes. See ADR-005.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded as an ADR with alternatives and consequences
Rationale addresses NAT/routing feasibility on each framework
Migration cost for the existing Arduino baselines is stated
Decision verified by direct inspection of the shipped core rather than by documentation claims

evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-005-firmware-framework-selection.md records the decision and the evidence that overturned the earlier ESP-IDF-first recommendation
ar t liblwip.a lists ip4_napt.c.obj; nm exports ip_napt_enable, ip_napt_enable_no, ip_napt_enable_netif, ip_napt_forward, ip_napt_recv
nm libesp_netif.a exports esp_netif_napt_enable and esp_netif_napt_disable
core sdkconfig: CONFIG_LWIP_IP_FORWARD=y, CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT=y, CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT_PORTMAP=y
verification.reason: Framework chosen and the decision rests on measured capability of the shipped core, not on documentation.

tasks.title: LwIP NAT forwarding between SoftAP clients and the active WAN
tasks.description: Implement packet forwarding and NAT translation between SoftAP clients and the active WAN. The RISK-002 dependency recorded here is now satisfied: TASK-020 proved PPP reaches phase RUNNING with a real CGNAT address, so the IP interface this task needs exists. NAPT is confirmed present in the shipped Arduino ESP32 core (liblwip.a contains ip4_napt.c.obj and exports ip_napt_enable_netif/ip_napt_forward/ip_napt_recv, and sdkconfig sets CONFIG_LWIP_IP_FORWARD, CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT and CONFIG_LWIP_IPV4_NAPT_PORTMAP), which is what removed the original ESP-IDF-only premise in ADR-005. Implementation note carried from the lwIP source: ip_napt_forward() returns early unless the INBOUND netif has napt set, so NAPT must be enabled on the SoftAP netif with the PPP netif as the outbound default route. ip_napt_enable_netif() is a no-op on a netif that is not yet up, so ordering is AP up first, then enable.
acceptance_criteria: A client associates with the SoftAP, receives a 192.168.4.x lease, and reaches the public internet through the LTE PPP WAN
NAPT is enabled on the SoftAP netif and the default route points at the PPP peer
The ESP32 gateway address is handed to clients as the DNS server so client name resolution traverses the NAT
Forwarding and translation are demonstrated with at least one client and evidenced from serial logs showing the client IP translated to the CGNAT address on egress
definition_of_done: Unit tests pass where logic exists
Project JSON and HTML updated and committed

tasks.title: Throughput and failover-time measurement harness
tasks.description: Measure actual NAT throughput and failover time and compare against the PRD NFRs of 10-15 Mbps and under 3 s. Produce evidence for a renegotiation decision. See RISK-001. Known ceiling to test: ip_napt_init() heap-allocates a fixed IP_NAPT_MAX=512 entry table (~16 KB via mem_calloc, not a memp pool) and ip_napt_init is not an exported symbol, so the table size cannot be raised without rebuilding lwIP. That caps concurrent translated connections and is a plausible cause of falling short of the throughput NFR.
acceptance_criteria: Measured NAT throughput in Mbps is recorded with the client count and LTE signal conditions stated alongside the figure
Measured failover time in seconds is recorded from loss of STA to successful client traffic via LTE
Both measurements are compared explicitly against the 10-15 Mbps and 3 s NFRs, and a short-fall is stated as a short-fall rather than a pass
If either NFR is missed, the NAPT entry-count ceiling and CPU/RAM headroom are reported as candidate causes and a renegotiation recommendation is made
definition_of_done: Unit tests pass where logic exists
Project JSON and HTML updated and committed
